value.title: fs3 Foundations
value.summary: Build the fs3 mold: workspace, DI architecture, drift enforcement, exemplars.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Plan 001 does not build fs3's features - it builds the mold the rest of fs3 is poured into: the cargo workspace implementing workshop 001's architecture (7 crates: core, parsers, providers, store, testkit, daemon, cli), full DI via exactly two trait ports (Embedder, Summarizer) wired at one composition root with config-driven provider selection including 'fake', a dockerized Postgres+pgvector compose stack, mechanical architecture-drift enforcement wired into harness checks, and one exemplar of every artifact kind later plans copy (pure-core unit test, port contract test, PG integration test, parser fixture test, build/check pipeline, docs shape). Exit bar: a fresh agent can implement any later feature by copying shapes already present, and architecture violations go red mechanically before review. Shipping this plan proves workshop 001's promotion-gate conditions 1-3; condition 4 (contract tests green over at least one REAL provider) needs an on-demand keyed run - the promotion move to docs/rules-idioms-architecture/ executes only once that run is recorded, else it is a named follow-up.

sections.name: goals
value: Cargo workspace with the 7-crate layout from workshop 001, compiling end-to-end at hello-world depth.
DI/IoC in the flesh: two trait ports, one composition root, config-driven provider selection including fake.
Architecture drift detected mechanically: crate-dependency allow-list check + clippy/fmt wired into harness checks.
Exemplar tests at every tier later plans copy: core unit (no doubles), port contract, PG integration, parser fixture.
Docker compose stack (Postgres+pgvector) and config loading from ~/.config/flowspace3.
README quick-start + docs/how/architecture.md signposted from README; harness boot healthy.

sections.name: non_goals
value: The real indexing pipeline (queue, watcher, scan) - plans 002+.
Search (semantic/text/regex), summaries, embeddings as real flows - later plans.
Conversations, MCP server, daemon web UI - later plans.
Real provider network calls as a gate requirement (fake providers suffice; real impls are compile-proven stubs).
The full tree-sitter grammar pack (parsers crate carries rust+markdown as the exemplar only).
flowspace3 doctor's full stack-repair flow (a ping/health exemplar stands in; doctor is a later plan).
Config hot-reload and per-worktree overrides (config loading lands; reload/override mechanics later).
Daemon containerization (PRD req 33's daemon-in-compose) - deferred: phase 1 runs the daemon on the host against composed PG; a later plan moves it into the compose stack.

value.claim: From a clean checkout, the documented steps yield green `cargo build --workspace` and `cargo test --workspace`.
The crate graph matches workshop 001 exactly; core compiles with no tokio/sqlx/HTTP dependencies.
The drift check FAILS when a forbidden dependency is added (negative test: add sqlx to core, check goes red, revert).
`docker compose up` brings Postgres+pgvector; the store integration test connects, applies migration 0001, and round-trips a row.
The daemon boots with fake providers selected via config from the flowspace3 config dir and serves GET /health on localhost; `flowspace3 ping` reports it healthy.
Exemplar tests pass at all tiers: core unit with zero doubles, Embedder contract over FakeEmbedder, PG integration; FakeEmbedder is deterministic (same text yields the same vector, asserted).
`harness checks` runs fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, tests, and the drift check, all green; `harness boot` reports healthy.
README carries the quick-start and signposts docs/how/architecture.md, which exists and reflects workshop 001.

sections.name: implementation_summary
sections.value: One phase. Order: workspace scaffold -> core (types, pure fns, ports) -> testkit fakes -> providers stub -> parsers exemplar -> compose+store -> config -> daemon -> cli -> drift check -> harness extensions -> docs -> evidence sweep. Every task's Done-When is mechanical (a command that passes or a file that exists with stated properties).

value.finding: POC: file discovery beats parser tuning (identical elements from 11% of bytes, 13.8x faster).
value.action: Foundations need no perf work; discovery filtering is a plan-002 concern (PRD req 41).

value.finding: POC: fs2's name-pattern classifier invents elements (C++ 58 claimed vs 22 real).

value.finding: sqlx compile-time query checks need a live DB or offline cache.

value.risk: Docker unavailable when tests run (CI or fresh machine)
value.mitigation: Integration tests detect missing docker and fail with the exact compose command; harness boot names it.

value.risk: Drift check too weak (passes things workshop 001 forbids)
value.mitigation: AC-03 negative test: deliberately violate, prove red, revert - the check's own exemplar.

value.risk: Exemplars over-engineered, becoming the very ceremony rule 3 refuses
value.mitigation: Each exemplar is the minimum that demonstrates the shape; review cites workshop 001's refused-list.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Workshop 001 is authoritative - do not contradict it; exactly two trait ports, a third is stop-and-ask.
core must not depend on tokio/sqlx/reqwest/axum; the drift check enforces the whole crate graph.
No mocking crates in any Cargo.toml; doubles come only from testkit.
Never hand-edit plan.dd.md / tasks.dd.md (generated).
Binary is flowspace3; config dir ~/.config/flowspace3 with FS3_CONFIG_DIR override for tests.
fs3 writes nothing outside the workspace, docs, and compose files (PRD req 39 spirit applies to this repo too).
